extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, and third-party requesters preparing or filing ex parte reexamination requests with the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing a USPTO request for ex parte reexamination of a patent, including required documents, substantive showings (substantial new question of patentability), and procedural formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed patent copy format and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the printed patent (including specification, drawings, and claims) must be supplied and reproduced on only one side of separate paper; two-sided copies are improper. Any disclaimer, certificate of correction, or reexamination certificate issued in the patent must also be supplied to provide the complete patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy must have each page plainly written on only one side. Include drawings, specification, and claims. Copies of any disclaimers, certificates of correction, or reexamination certificates that are part of the patent must be provided so the Office has the complete patent file copy (see MPEP § 2219).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of service on patent owner (when requester is not owner)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request is filed by a person other than the patent owner, include a certification that a copy of the request has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the address provided in 37 CFR 1.33(c), indicating the name and address of the party served and the date of service (or provide a duplicate copy to the Office if service was not possible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service was not possible after a reasonable effort, supply a duplicate copy to the Office together with a cover letter explaining efforts made and why service failed. To avoid erroneous duplicate filing-fee charges, requesters are strongly encouraged to clearly label such cover letters (e.g., bold heading: "Duplicate Copy of Request Filed under 37 CFR 1.510(b)(5) When Service on the Patent Owner Was Not Possible").

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment and completeness to obtain filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a reexamination filing date the request papers must include the fee required by 37 CFR 1.510(a) (and any applicable excess-claim fees) and satisfy all parts required by 37 CFR 1.510(b); requests failing these requirements are incomplete and will not be granted a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entire fee under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1) must be paid. If the fee is not paid or requirements not satisfied, the requester will be notified and given a chance to complete the request; failure to comply results in no filing date and placement of the papers in the patent file as a citation if they meet 37 CFR 1.501 standards. Filing date is the date on which the request satisfies all requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content: statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability (37 CFR 1.510(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The detailed request must include a statement identifying each substantial new question of patentability based on prior patents and printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must clearly set forth in detail what the requester considers the "substantial new question of patentability" to be in view of prior patents and printed publications and must point out how any questions raised are substantially different from those raised during earlier examination(s). It is not sufficient merely to propose rejections; the reference(s) relied upon must present a new, non-cumulative technological teaching not previously considered and discussed on the record, unless old art is presented in a new light with a material new argument/interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content: identification of claims and detailed explanation applying cited art (37 CFR 1.510(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must identify every claim for which reexamination is requested and include a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior patents and printed publications to each such claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide limitation-by-limitation explanations—ideally in a detailed claim chart—showing how each claimed limitation maps to the teachings of each reference. For each proposed combination explain how each reference is used and provide at least one basis for combining references for obviousness rejections. Quote pertinent teachings and cite page/column/line numbers and figure numbers where appropriate. Avoid lumping claims or proposed combinations together; use clear, specific language (examples of inappropriate and appropriate phrasing are provided in the MPEP). Any failure to provide required explanations will result in a Notice of Failure to Comply and possible withdrawal or need to cure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art limited to patents and printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial new questions of patentability in reexamination must be based on prior patents and printed publications (statutory prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102/103).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters such as public use, on-sale, inventorship, 35 U.S.C. 101, 35 U.S.C. 112, conduct by parties, etc., should not be included in the request and will not be considered when making the determination on the request. A cited patent/printed publication cannot be used merely as evidence of alleged public use or on-sale activity; it must be applied directly to claims under appropriate portions of 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of previously considered (old) art only when presented in a new light
rubrics_metrics.description: Art previously cited to or considered by the Office may raise a substantial new question of patentability only if it is presented/viewed in a new light or different way with a material new argument or interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2002 Act permits SNQs based on old art, but the request must present the old art in a manner that raises new questions about pre-existing technology (e.g., a material new analysis). Reexamination requests relying only on the Supreme Court's KSR clarification without presenting the art in a new light will not raise a SNQ. The SNQ standard remains unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness combination requirement (basis for combining)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed obviousness rejections, the requester must provide at least one clear basis for combining the cited references and explain why the claim(s) would have been obvious over the proposed combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably quote pertinent teachings from each reference and provide citations to specific pages/cols/lines and figures. Do not lump multiple alternative combinations together without explaining the distinct rationale for each combination. Examples of acceptable and unacceptable phrasing are provided in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of explanation and cure/withdrawal procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The explanation applying art to claims must be complete; if any document/combination/claim lacks explanation the Office will issue a Notice of Failure to Comply identifying the deficiencies and the requester must either provide separate explanations for each deficiency or explicitly withdraw the deficient documents/claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requester withdraws claims or references identified in the notice, no explanation is required for withdrawn items and the request will proceed only for the remaining claims/references. If the defects are not cured, the request will be considered incomplete and may not receive a filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits, declarations, and other written evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, declarations, or other written evidence that explain the contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents or printed publications may be considered in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such evidence can be used to clarify or establish dates/contents of cited references when necessary (see MPEP § 2258).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PTO/SB/57 transmittal form—use and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/57 is the recommended transmittal/cover sheet for filing a request for ex parte reexamination but its use is encouraged not mandatory; the form collects requester identity, fee/payment authorization, copy of patent, sequence listing formats, and other filing information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form includes fields to indicate requester type (patent owner or third party), requester name/address, payment method (check, deposit account, or credit card via PTO-2038), refund instructions, a checkbox that a copy of the patent is enclosed (double-column format on one side), inclusion of CD-ROMs or sequence listings if applicable, inclusion of copies of disclaimers/corrections, identification of claims for reexamination, listing/all copies of every patent or printed publication relied upon, English translations of non-English references, certification of service or duplicate copy, correspondence address, and concurrent proceedings. Warning: do not include credit card details on this form (use PTO-2038).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing and special material submission formats
rubrics_metrics.description: If nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence listings or large tables/computer program appendices are submitted, they must be provided in the required computer readable forms and media (e.g., CD-ROM/CD-R copies and paper as applicable) with statements verifying identity of the copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable media include CD-ROM or CD-R (in duplicate) or other specified formats; include verification statements confirming identity of the copies and follow the MPEP guidance for sequence submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translations for non-English references
rubrics_metrics.description: An English language translation of all necessary and pertinent non-English language patents and/or printed publications must be included with the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations should cover the portions of the references relied upon so the Office and patent owner can assess the cited material's pertinency and application to the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed amendment permitted only for patent owner requester
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed amendment to the patent may be included in the request only when the patent owner is the requester (see 37 CFR 1.510(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner files the request and includes a proposed amendment, additional excess-claims fees may apply under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) as described in MPEP § 2250.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) not permitted in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.76 cannot be submitted in a reexamination proceeding because a reexamination proceeding is not an 'application.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to submit ADS forms in reexamination filings; include required information via the prescribed reexamination transmittal form and supporting papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of every patent/printed publication relied upon must be submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon for the request must be submitted with the request, including a listing thereof on Form PTO/SB/08, PTO-1449, or equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply full copies (and translations where necessary) for each reference so the examiner and patent owner can evaluate the basis for the requested reexamination; failure to supply copies can lead to deficiency notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural and public disclosure considerations (privacy and disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information submitted on the transmittal form may become public and is subject to Freedom of Information Act and Privacy Act rules; certain routine uses and possible disclosures are outlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware personal and filing information may be disclosed as part of public records (e.g., upon publication or issuance of patent) and in other routine uses (e.g., disclosures to DOJ, contractors, other agencies). Do not include credit card information on the form; use PTO-2038 for payment authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds and placement of incomplete requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request is denied or vacated a refund will be made in accordance with 37 CFR 1.26(c); if a request is incomplete and the defect is not cured a refund will be made in accordance with 37 CFR 1.26(a). If defects remain and fee unpaid, request papers may be placed in the patent file as a citation under 37 CFR 1.501.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester is given an opportunity to supply missing items (including fees) and fails to do so, no determination will be made and the papers may be treated as a citation. See MPEP §§ 2227, 2247, and 2246 for denial/vacatur/refund handling.
